head: 58ff51feb

boundaries: the spec against the API origin

notes: The per-run E2E flake. One pass, no finding. G4 rebuilt k5e-signed-in-e2e-covered-by-key-step, which this change made stale.

instruments.evidence: 58ff51feb: omnigame-launch.spec.ts answers every API call its tests do not mock with a 404, and waits for the signed-in user instead of polling a localStorage auth_token. Boundary: the spec against the API origin (a real server in CI's E2E job and in a local stack).
Read 5ba782a38 (K5e: the signed-in spec covered by the key step, control k5e-signed-in-e2e-covered-by-key-step) and 065c6b6c5 (which recorded the local failure at base). Neither found the 401 dialog.

instruments.why: No prompt or payload is built.

instruments.evidence: Printed every request that reaches the new 404 route, for both tests. Guest: GET /auth/me x4 (the app treats it as signed out, as it did the 401). Signed-in: GET /feature-flags, /conversations, /users/me/friends/requests, POST /auth/ws-token, /users/me/ping x2, /logs/frontend. None opens a dialog; page errors are two 404 lines only.
CI's E2E step sets VITE_API_URL=http://localhost:8080/api/v1 (ci.yml:339); the route pattern is http://localhost:8080/api/v1/**, so it matches in CI as it does locally.
The test's own routes (auth/me, key-backup, launch) are registered after the fallback, so Playwright tries them first; the signed-in run shows neither auth/me nor key-backup reaching the fallback.
The API client's contract: api.ts:78 opens the sign-in dialog on any 401 except /auth/me and /auth/logout; a 404 takes the toast path only. The fix relies on exactly that.
The fallback body has the shape the server uses for errors (error, message).
Both tests in the file get the fallback; the guest test had the same exposure for any 401 a guest call can get.
Unmocked calls still show as 404 console errors, so a test that starts depending on one is visible.
The CORS header set repeats omnichat.spec's corsHeaders; two spec files, left separate rather than adding a shared helper for one reuse.

Every spec that fakes a signed-in user: omnigame-launch and e2e/omnichat. omnichat already routes all of localhost:8080/api/v1/** and answers unknown paths with 500, which opens no dialog. No other instance.
No finding. The change's own check: with the fallback removed, 3 of 5 runs failed on the z-50 sign-in overlay; with it, 20 of 20 passed with the real backend up.
The spec runs in CI E2E on every push touching frontend.
eslint and prettier clean on the spec; hook checks passed on commit.
No model output. Ran the real app against a real backend, which is how the failure was reproduced.
The spec still refuses a broken flow: k5e control (account without a device key) makes the signed-in test time out behind the key step.
Playwright counts read from the output: 20 passed, none skipped.
The user asked to fix the flaky E2E test; the cause is found and removed, and the old poll that proved nothing is gone.
Only the spec changed; it was run in full.
Ran the changed signed-in spec 10 times each test, real backend up: 20/20.

k5e-signed-in-e2e-covered-by-key-step patched this spec and no longer applied (its context line now sits beside answerUnmockedApiCalls). Rebuilt on HEAD: removing the device key and key-backup route fails the signed-in test, 3 attempts, 'key-step-title dialog intercepts pointer events'.
The spec runs the real app in a real browser.

gates.tests: omnigame-launch 20/20 with a real backend; k5e control fails as expected
